claim: On a plain incline, momentum's step grows towards ε·c/(1 − μ), ten times plain descent's ε·c at μ = 0.9: the known reason momentum crosses a gentle slope faster.
derivation: On f = c·x, ∇f = c everywhere, so v_{k} = μ·v_{k−1} − ε·c from v_0 = 0.
Summing the geometric series: v_k = −ε·c·(1 − μ^k)/(1 − μ), which tends to −ε·c/(1 − μ).
With ε = 0.1, μ = 0.9, c = 1, θ_0 = 0, k = 50, by exact fractions.
